meta.title: Can the Cangjie Skill turn long content into actionable skills?
meta.summary: It breaks down books, long videos, and podcasts into callable skills, but free code does not mean the entire process is cost-free.

pageProps.markdownHtml:
Info: Machine translation This post was machine-translated from the Chinese original. Wording may be rough in places — the Chinese version is authoritative.

Collecting a book, a long video, or a podcast often results in not learning but lying into “I’ll read later.” Cangjie Skill aims to solve this gap: not just compressing content, but organizing reusable methods, processes, and judgment rules into skills that Agents can call based on scenarios.

What it delivers is not a summary

Cangjie Skill is designed for books, long-form video transcripts, podcast transcripts, courses, interviews, long articles, and resource collections. It first forms a capability source and then compiles it into installable skill products; The project explicitly excludes ordinary book excerpts, book reflections, and author role-playing.

You can think of a regular summary as a courier SMS: it tells you roughly what’s in the package. The Cangjie Skill is more like sorting goods onto a shelf, then marking which tasks to go to which location, how to use them, and when it’s not applicable. The focus is not just on “remembering content,” but on having the Agent find and execute the methods in subsequent tasks.

  • Global understanding: generate BOOK_OVERVIEW.md that retains the main idea, structure, terminology, and critical analysis.
  • Capability organization: Write validated methods into the Capability Bundle and capability cards, and record dependencies, comparisons, and combinations between capabilities.
  • Installable products: can be compiled into single mode with a single routing entry point, or a pack mode with “routing entry + a few independent skills.”
  • Acceptance materials: Retain coverage audits, items to be verified, reasons for obsolescence, test cases, DIGEST.md, and operational records.

Which clients and environments are available

The repository’s README clearly lists OpenClaw, Claude Code, and DeepSeek Harness; DeepSeek Harness also includes plugin installation packages adapted for v2.5.0. The repository does not declare in this document that Codex has completed compatibility verification, so it cannot be written as running on Codex based solely on the filename or directory format.

Project Explanations in the materials Use the front boundary
OpenClaw The README lists the supported platforms This is the author’s statement; no runtime verification was conducted this time
Claude Code The README lists the supported platforms This is the author’s statement; no runtime verification was conducted this time
DeepSeek Harness Provides standalone plugin installation packages You need to have DeepSeek Harness first and verify the downloaded package
Deterministic script Python 3.10+ and PyYAML are required tiktoken and jsonschema are optional dependencies

Warning “Author lists supported platforms” does not mean all versions, operating systems, and clients are independently operational. Before officially entering the workflow, a publicly available and controllable material should be test-run, and check whether the product can be recognized and called by the target client.

How to start so you don’t go off track right away

  • Prepare the full text: it can be PDF, EPUB, TXT, subtitles, or transcripts. When there is no accessible text, the project requires stopping instead of generating from memory.
  • Complete meta information: Books need title, author, and publication year; Videos, podcasts, or courses require titles, authors or speakers, and publication dates for traceability.
  • Intended purpose: For learning and consulting, prefer singles; For daily workflows and cross-content combinations, packs are more preferred.
  • The first time you try only one item: first confirm the extraction quality, call method, and test results, then decide whether to batch process.

The author’s RIA-TV++ process first understands the entire material, then uses different extractors to find frameworks, principles, cases, counterexamples, and terminology; Candidate content is then checked for source adequacy, feasibility, and task gain, before deciding whether to become an independent skill or remain in a unified routing portal. Finally, representative task testing, compilation, and delivery are also performed.

The free code is not all upstream and running costs

The repository code is licensed under the MIT License and can be used, copied, modified, merged, published, distributed, sublicensed, and sold for free, but copyright and license notices must be retained; The software is provided “as is” without warranty.

This does not automatically make the entire workflow zero-cost. Running it still requires a compatible Agent environment, Python 3.10+, and PyYAML; When processing videos or podcasts, subtitles, transcriptions, or other available text must be obtained first. Whether the model, cloud services, and content acquisition segments called by the Agent are charged must be checked separately and cannot be deduced from the MIT license in the repository.

Warning The MIT license covers the software and documentation in the repository and does not automatically grant redistribution rights for input books, courses, videos, podcasts, and their materials. After distilling copyrighted content into a skill, whether it can be publicly distributed must be separately verified under the original content’s licensing scope.

Its value lies in the process; the real results still have to be evaluated by oneself

This project not only provides prompts but also describes steps such as capability cards, coverage audits, stress testing, compilation, snapshots, rollbacks, and manual modification detection. It aims to solve consistency and traceability in skill production, rather than having Agents casually summarize and announce completion.

The snapshot records the repository with 11,055 stars and 1,285 forks, created on April 16, 2026, and last pushed on October 2, 2026; The license is MIT, and the repository is not forked, archived, or disabled. The star snapshot also records an increase from 11,007 to 11,055 in 1.1 days, but this observation window only shows changes during that period and cannot replace long-term trend judgment or feature quality verification.

Warning This time, only the README, SKILL.md, license, and repository status were verified; no scripts were executed, and no end-to-end testing was completed on any client. The sample warehouses listed by the author can illustrate the expected product form and cannot be impersonated as independent reproduction results, security audits, or compatibility certifications.

Who is worth trying?

  • Suitable for: Those who already have a legally usable long text and want to integrate the methodology into the Agent workflow, rather than just a summary.
  • Suitable for: Those willing to check sources, boundaries, trigger conditions, and test results, and willing to pilot with a single piece of material first.
  • Not suitable for those who only have video links without subtitles or transcription and want tools to restore the entire content out of thin air.
  • Not suitable for now: Those who only want to imitate the author’s personality or plan to publicly distribute generated results without review.

The safest starting point is to choose a material with clear copyright boundaries, familiar to you, and able to verify the original text, and use a single-model small-scale pilot. During acceptance, don’t just look at whether the file has been generated; randomly select several abilities to verify sources, trigger conditions, execution steps, failure boundaries, and actual task results. Only when all these match can the Cangjie Skill transform from a “document organization project” into a truly usable workflow.

  • kangarooking/cangjie-skill project repository
